#Module frames

Nested browsing contexts for JavaScript (src/page/frames.odin, frames_scripts.odin; native/js/runtime/frames.c and prelude/frames.js). A window of another document is named by its navigable's id: each document runs in its own engine instance, so another window is a WindowProxy of the calling realm that only reaches what HTML lets a cross-origin window reach (postMessage, location as a setter, closed, frames, length, top, parent, opener, window, self, close, focus, blur); documents never share objects, same origin or not.

Exposed to: Window. Source: api/frames.widl.

The navigable of the calling document.

#Frame_ofElement

u64 Frame_ofElement(u64 element)

The navigable of a frame element (<iframe>, <frame>) of the calling document; 0 when it has none (not connected, frames off).

Host: Frame_ofElement :: proc(c: ^Call, element: u64) -> u64

u64 Frame_parent(u64 navigable)

The parent navigable; 0 for a top-level one, or one that is gone.

Host: Frame_parent :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64) -> u64

u64 Frame_top(u64 navigable)

The top-level navigable of its tab; 0 when it is gone.

Host: Frame_top :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64) -> u64

How many child navigables its document has (window.length).

#Frame_sameOrigin

Whether its document is same origin with the calling one.

#Frame_postMessage

void Frame_postMessage(u64 navigable, bytes data, usvstring target_origin) raises

otherWindow.postMessage(message, targetOrigin): data is the message's structured serialization (runtime/clone.c); target_origin is "*", "/" or a URL. The message is delivered from a task of the target's, if its document's origin then matches. Syntax for an invalid target origin, Data_Clone for a message over frames.max_message_bytes.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_postMessage :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, data: []u8, target_origin: string) -> Api_Error

#Frame_navigate

void Frame_navigate(u64 navigable, usvstring url, bool replace) raises

otherWindow.location = url, location.href = url, location.replace(url): Security when the calling document may not navigate it (HTML "allowed to navigate", the sandbox; the console says why), Syntax for an invalid URL.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_navigate :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, url: string, replace: bool) -> Api_Error

#Frame_open

u64 Frame_open(usvstring url, string target) raises

window.open(url, target): a frame's name, _self, _parent or _top is navigated and its navigable returned; any other target opens a new tab (when the embedder can) and gives 0 (no opener relationship, as noopener). Not_Allowed in a sandboxed document without allow-popups, Syntax for an invalid URL.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_open :: proc(c: ^Call, url: string, target: string) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#Frame_postMessagePorts

void Frame_postMessagePorts(u64 navigable, bytes data, usvstring target_origin, u64[] ports) raises

otherWindow.postMessage(message, targetOrigin, [ports]): the same, with the MessagePorts of the transfer list shipped as port ends (Port_ship / Port_entangle): the receiver's MessageEvent.ports are bound to them.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_postMessagePorts :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, data: []u8, target_origin: string, ports: []u64) -> Api_Error

#Window_get_name

string Window_get_name()

window.name: its navigable's name.

Host: Window_get_name :: proc(c: ^Call) -> string

#Window_set_name

void Window_set_name(string value)

window.name = value

Host: Window_set_name :: proc(c: ^Call, value: string)
